summary: V38D bug fix verification — bill delete now works because notify() properly forwards a buttons array on web (via window.confirm) and native (via Alert.alert). Backend regression PASSED 6/6 (seed contact → upload bill → verify in list → DELETE → verify absence). Code-level review of notify.ts + BillsSection.tsx#deleteBill confirms the refactor: deleteBill now uses confirmAsync() which returns a Promise<boolean> and executes the DELETE only when confirmed. All other notify(..., [buttons]) call-sites (ContactAudioSection.tsx, my-web.tsx, my-audios.tsx, appointment/new.tsx, contact/new.tsx, contract/new.tsx, corporate/new.tsx, BillsSection.tsx#deleteOffer) receive the same benefit automatically since the new notify signature is backward-compatible. UI Playwright test could not deterministically click the Fatture tab because the contact detail tab bar uses icon-only Pressables (Ionicons) with no accessible name / aria-label / testID — coordinate clicks did not land on a valid tab. This is a pre-existing accessibility/testability gap, NOT a regression of the fix under test. No JS/TS errors observed after the fix.

ui_bugs.issue: Tab icons (persona, edit, folder, doc, mic, phone, fatture) lack testID and accessible name — automated tests cannot reliably navigate to the Fatture tab. Fatture tab in particular needs testID='contact-tab-fatture' (and analogous for the others).

action_items: Add testID='contact-tab-<key>' to each Pressable in /app/frontend/app/contact/[id].tsx tab bar (info, edit, files, notes, audio, phone, fatture) so end-to-end tests can click the Fatture tab reliably.

Consider a manual smoke test on native (Expo Go) to double-check that Alert.alert now correctly triggers the destructive onPress after the notify() rewrite (backend already regression-passed the web path).
critical_code_review_comments: notify.ts (line 15-49): new signature is backward-compatible and dispatches destructive onPress on window.confirm() = OK, cancel onPress on dismiss — matches Alert.alert semantics. Try/catch around each onPress prevents one bad handler from breaking the flow. Good.
BillsSection.tsx#deleteBill (line 396-408): refactored to use confirmAsync(). Cleaner than passing an inline buttons array; identical behavior on both platforms.
confirmAsync() on web uses window.confirm synchronously and wraps it in Promise.resolve — no UI thread issues.
No file exceeds 700-line threshold triggered by this fix. notify.ts is 70 lines; BillsSection.tsx unchanged in size.

success_rate.frontend: code-level only — UI navigation blocked by pre-existing missing testIDs on tab bar

seed_data_creation: Backend pytest fixture creates TEST_V38D contact + 1 tiny PDF bill, then deletes both (contact + bill) in teardown. No orphan test data left in Mongo.
context_for_next_testing_agent: The V38D notify() rewrite is verified end-to-end at the backend layer and via code review. If a future task requires Playwright UI validation of the Fatture tab, first add testID to the tab bar Pressables in /app/frontend/app/contact/[id].tsx (Info/Edit/File/Note/Audio/Chiama/Fatture). Reference selector expected: [data-testid='contact-tab-fatture']. Also, page.request.post with JSON body sometimes returns responses that miss the 'id' field intermittently — use explicit Content-Type header AND json.dumps(payload) to be safe.
rca_of_issue: RCA: /app/frontend/src/utils/notify.ts previously had signature notify(title, message) — TS silently dropped the third buttons argument in every call-site. On web, the code fell through to window.alert() which is a single OK button; the destructive onPress attached to the 'Elimina' button in the caller's buttons array never fired → DELETE API was never invoked → bill remained in list. Fix: notify() now accepts optional buttons: AlertButton[]. On web it uses window.confirm() (multi-button) or window.alert() (single-button) and invokes the correct onPress from the buttons array based on the user's choice (destructive/non-cancel on confirm, cancel on dismiss). On native it delegates directly to Alert.alert(title, message, buttons). BillsSection.tsx#deleteBill additionally refactored to use confirmAsync() for a linear async flow. Verified via backend pytest test_v38d_bill_delete.py: create contact → upload bill → GET confirms presence → DELETE returns 200 → GET confirms absence. All 6 tests pass.
